items.entity: Design domain Ω (shape and aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 only refers to 'the full design domain Ω', and the domain itself is drawn in Fig. 1, which is not available. The text gives no dimensions or aspect ratio. The only size hint is the 64×64 dataset images in Sec. 4.1, and the text does not say that Fig. 1 follows the dataset conventions.
readings: Square domain, aspect 1:1 (like the 64×64 dataset images)

items.description: No mesh is given for Fig. 1; Sec. 2.1 only says SIMP gives a density to 'every element of the mesh'. Sec. 4.1 uses 64×64 images, but it does not say whether Fig. 1 uses that size. It also does not say whether 64×64 counts elements or nodes: the load channels give a value to 'every node', while the first channel is the topology image.
readings: 64×64 square Q4 elements (65×65 nodes), matching the dataset image size
63×63 elements (64×64 nodes, if image pixels are nodes)
128×64 elements if a 2:1 domain is adopted

items.entity: Displacement boundary conditions (where they are applied)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 says displacement boundary conditions are applied on nodes, and the Fig. 1 caption only mentions 'boundary conditions'. Their location and extent appear only in Fig. 1. Sec. 4.1 mentions 42 (+5) boundary-condition scenarios but never lists them.
readings: Two bottom corner nodes (x = 0 and x = L at y = 0)
Left edge as symmetry line + bottom-right corner node (half-MBB)
Partial edge segment, e.g. bottom edge 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.25L

items.entity: Restrained displacement components at the supports
items.description: The text does not say which displacement components are fixed (clamp or roller). The Fig. 2 caption says boundary conditions are drawn as 'color lines and dots', which suggests the restrained direction is colour-coded in the figures, but the text gives no legend.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at all support nodes
Pin (u_x = u_y = 0) at one support and roller (u_y = 0) at the other

items.description: The Fig. 1 caption only says 'a given set of load'; the load's location is drawn in the figure. Sec. 4.1 says dataset loads go on randomly chosen unconstrained boundary nodes, so any free boundary node is possible.

Sec. 2.1 says 'loads applied on the nodes', the Fig. 1 caption says 'a given set of load', and the Fig. 2 caption says 'the load applied'. Whether Fig. 1 has one concentrated force, several forces or a spread load is shown only in the figure.
readings: Single concentrated force at one boundary node
Two or more concentrated forces at different boundary nodes acting simultaneously
Force spread over a few adjacent boundary nodes

items.description: No direction is given for Fig. 1; the arrow is only in the figure. Sec. 4.1 limits dataset directions to [0, π] in π/6 steps but defines neither the reference axis nor the sense of rotation. For a single load, flipping the sign does not change compliance, but the line of action does.

Sec. 2.1, the Fig. 1 caption and Sec. 4.1 give no force magnitude. With a single load, the magnitude only scales compliance. If there are several loads, their relative magnitudes would also matter (see the load-count item).
The Fig. 1 caption lists a volume fraction as an input, but the text gives no value. Sec. 4.1 only says dataset values lie in [0.3, 0.5] with a step of 0.02.
Neither Sec. 2.1 nor the dataset description (Sec. 4.1, ToPy) gives an elastic modulus or thickness.
Poisson's ratio is not given anywhere in the text.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The text does not state whether the analysis is plane stress or plane strain, which changes the effective Poisson's ratio. The only hint is that the von Mises formula in Sec. 4.1 is the plane-stress form, and that applies to the dataset, not explicitly to Fig. 1.
Sec. 2.1 only says SIMP uses a penalization factor 'with p > 1'. No value or continuation scheme is given, and the ToPy settings in Sec. 4.1 are not given either.
Sec. 1 and Sec. 2.1 mention filters used to avoid grey pixels and encourage binary densities. They give no filter type, radius or projection parameters.
readings: Density filter + Heaviside projection with β continuation

items.entity: Optimizer, initial design and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 2.1 only says SIMP is gradient-based and tends to converge to local optima, so these choices can change the result. Sec. 4.1 names ToPy for the dataset, but no update scheme, move limit, starting design or convergence tolerance is given.
readings: OC update (move limit 0.2, damping 0.5), uniform start ρ = VF, stop when max density change < 0.01
OC with a fixed iteration count (e.g. 100)
MMA, uniform start ρ = VF, stop when max density change < 0.01

items.description: The lower bound on density or stiffness for void elements, needed by SIMP (Sec. 2.1), is not stated.

items.entity: Post-processing / binarization of the final design
items.description: Fig. 1 shows an 'optimal structure', and Sec. 4.1 calls the SIMP result a 'black and white image'. No thresholding rule is given, which matters if the shown design or its compliance is to be reproduced.
readings: Volume-preserving threshold that meets the target volume fraction

items.description: No passive regions are mentioned for Fig. 1. The load-violation metric in Sec. 4.2 requires material wherever a load acts. That could be enforced with solid passive elements or left to the optimizer.
readings: Solid passive element(s) at the loaded node(s)
Solid passive elements at the loaded node(s) and at the supports
